## 1. Idea

Experiment 0 showed that a dense genomic kernel (GBLUP) beats every screened method on FT10, so
screening *alone* loses signal. But screening is good at one thing a dense ridge is not: it
finds large-effect SNPs. This experiment keeps the dense kernel and adds TARP's own step 1
(Bernoulli RIS screening) as a second kernel:

    K = K_full + w * K_screened

Each SNP has prior variance proportional to 1/p; screened SNPs get an extra w/p_screened, i.e. a
prior-variance boost of about `1 + w * p / p_screened` (about 196 w for ~8.7k screened SNPs).
`w = 0` is exactly GBLUP; very large `w` approaches screened-only ridge.

**Honest protocol.** `w` and lambda are chosen by nested CV in which the screening is redone
inside every inner fold, so the validation rows never influenced the screened set (the lesson of
Experiments 1 and 1b). The outer test set is touched only at the end. Same seeds, splits and
outer screened sets as every earlier run.

```{r blas-fix}
if (!requireNamespace("RhpcBLASctl", quietly = TRUE)) {
  stop("Run in terminal first: micromamba install -c conda-forge r-rhpcblasctl")
}
RhpcBLASctl::blas_set_num_threads(1)
N_CORES <- 3
N_REPS <- 10
K_IN <- 5
LAM_GRID <- 10^seq(-3, 3, length.out = 61)
W_GRID <- c(0, 0.003, 0.01, 0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3)
stopifnot(W_GRID[1] == 0)
mem_check <- function(label) {
  g <- gc(full = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("[memory] %s: %.0f MB in use\n", label, sum(g[, 2])))
}
```

```{r load-once}
library(bigsnpr); library(bigstatsr)
obj.bigSNP <- snp_attach("arabidopsis_1135_matched.rds")
G <- obj.bigSNP$genotypes; map <- obj.bigSNP$map; fam <- obj.bigSNP$fam
pheno <- read.csv("flowering_time.csv")
y_all <- pheno$FT10[match(as.character(fam$sample.ID), as.character(pheno$accession_id))]
n <- nrow(G); p <- ncol(G)
G2 <- snp_fastImputeSimple(G, method = "mean2", ncores = N_CORES)

gr <- readRDS("gram_full_snp.rds"); Kfull <- gr$K        # built in Experiment 0
stopifnot(nrow(Kfull) == n)
cat("Loaded full-SNP Gram matrix:", dim(Kfull), "\n")
mem_check("after loading")
```

## 2. Helpers

```{r helpers}
# TARP step 1 using ONLY the given training rows: marginal correlation -> |r|^delta -> Bernoulli draw
screen_set <- function(tr_rows, y_tr_vec) {
  gw <- big_univLinReg(G2, y.train = y_tr_vec, ind.train = tr_rows, ncores = N_CORES)
  tt <- gw$estim / gw$std.err
  r <- sign(tt) * sqrt(tt^2 / (tt^2 + (length(tr_rows) - 2))); r[is.na(r)] <- 0
  delta <- max(0, (1 + log(p / length(tr_rows))) / 2)
  q_in <- abs(r)^delta; q_in <- q_in / max(q_in)
  list(inc = which(rbinom(p, 1, q_in) == 1), r = r)
}

# n x n kernel of the screened SNPs over ALL rows; standardized with all rows (no y involved),
# matching how K_full was built
screened_gram <- function(inc) {
  Xs <- G2[, inc]
  cs <- apply(Xs, 2, sd); keep <- cs > 0
  Xs <- scale(Xs[, keep, drop = FALSE], center = TRUE, scale = cs[keep])
  tcrossprod(Xs) / sum(keep)
}

# kernel ridge predictions of the centered response for EVERY lambda from one eigendecomposition
kernel_curve <- function(K, K_new, y_c, lam_grid) {
  eg <- eigen(K, symmetric = TRUE); e <- pmax(eg$values, 0); U <- eg$vectors
  yt <- as.numeric(crossprod(U, y_c))
  K_new %*% (U %*% (yt / outer(e, lam_grid, "+")))
}
mse_curve <- function(pred_c, y_new_c) colMeans((y_new_c - pred_c)^2)
```

## 3. One replication

```{r replication-fn}
run_rep <- function(seed_i) {
  set.seed(seed_i)                                            # same RNG path as every earlier run
  train_idx <- sample(seq_len(n), size = round(0.8 * n))
  test_idx  <- setdiff(seq_len(n), train_idx)
  y_tr <- y_all[train_idx]; y_te <- y_all[test_idx]; y_mean <- mean(y_tr)
  sc <- screen_set(train_idx, y_tr)                           # outer screening (identical to before)
  Ks_all <- screened_gram(sc$inc)

  set.seed(seed_i * 1000 + 7)                                 # separate stream for inner folds
  fold <- sample(rep(seq_len(K_IN), length.out = length(train_idx)))
  cv <- array(0, c(K_IN, length(W_GRID), length(LAM_GRID)))
  for (f in seq_len(K_IN)) {
    in_tr <- train_idx[fold != f]; in_va <- train_idx[fold == f]
    y_in <- y_all[in_tr]; ym <- mean(y_in)
    sf <- screen_set(in_tr, y_in)                             # re-screen INSIDE the fold
    Ks_f <- screened_gram(sf$inc)
    for (iw in seq_along(W_GRID)) {
      w <- W_GRID[iw]
      Ktr <- Kfull[in_tr, in_tr] + w * Ks_f[in_tr, in_tr]
      Kva <- Kfull[in_va, in_tr] + w * Ks_f[in_va, in_tr]
      cv[f, iw, ] <- mse_curve(kernel_curve(Ktr, Kva, y_in - ym, LAM_GRID), y_all[in_va] - ym)
    }
  }
  cvm <- apply(cv, c(2, 3), mean)                             # W x L
  jl_w <- apply(cvm, 1, which.min)                            # best lambda for each w
  best <- arrayInd(which.min(cvm), dim(cvm)); iw_star <- best[1, 1]; il_star <- best[1, 2]

  te <- t(vapply(seq_along(W_GRID), function(iw) {            # outer fit, test MSPE for every (w, lambda)
    w <- W_GRID[iw]
    Ktr <- Kfull[train_idx, train_idx] + w * Ks_all[train_idx, train_idx]
    Kte <- Kfull[test_idx, train_idx]  + w * Ks_all[test_idx, train_idx]
    mse_curve(kernel_curve(Ktr, Kte, y_tr - y_mean, LAM_GRID), y_te - y_mean)
  }, numeric(length(LAM_GRID))))                              # W x L

  out <- data.frame(seed = seed_i, n_screened = length(sc$inc),
                    TwoK_honest = te[iw_star, il_star],       # the method: (w, lambda) chosen by nested CV
                    GBLUP_nested = te[1, jl_w[1]],            # w = 0 with lambda chosen the same way
                    TwoK_oracle = min(te),                    # diagnostic only: peeks at the test set
                    w_sel = W_GRID[iw_star], lam_sel = LAM_GRID[il_star], cv_min = min(cvm))
  for (iw in seq_along(W_GRID)) out[[paste0("T_w", W_GRID[iw])]] <- te[iw, jl_w[iw]]
  out
}
```

## 4. Run with checkpointing (use tmux; roughly 1.5-2 minutes per seed)

```{r run}
ckpt <- "exp3_results.rds"
res_list <- if (file.exists(ckpt)) readRDS(ckpt) else list()
cat("Resuming with", length(res_list), "reps done\n")
for (i in seq_len(N_REPS)) {
  if (i <= length(res_list) && !is.null(res_list[[i]])) next
  t0 <- Sys.time()
  res_list[[i]] <- run_rep(i)
  saveRDS(res_list, ckpt)
  r_ <- res_list[[i]]
  cat(sprintf("Rep %d/%d (%.1f min) | GBLUP_nested %.1f  TwoK_honest %.1f (w=%s)  | oracle %.1f\n",
              i, N_REPS, as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "mins")),
              r_$GBLUP_nested, r_$TwoK_honest, r_$w_sel, r_$TwoK_oracle))
  mem_check(paste("rep", i))
}
all_res <- do.call(rbind, res_list)
```

## 5. Merge with earlier experiments and compare

```{r summary}
prev <- do.call(rbind, readRDS("si_replication_results.rds"))
m <- match(all_res$seed, prev$seed)
cat("screened counts identical to earlier runs:", all(all_res$n_screened == prev$n_screened[m]), "\n")
all_res$RP_agg_old <- prev$RP_agg[m]
if (file.exists("exp0_results.rds")) {
  e0 <- readRDS("exp0_results.rds"); all_res$GBLUP_loo <- e0$Lin_loo[match(all_res$seed, e0$seed)]
}
if (file.exists("exp1b_results.rds")) {
  e1b <- do.call(rbind, readRDS("exp1b_results.rds"))
  all_res$Screened_lin_honest <- e1b$Lin_honest[match(all_res$seed, e1b$seed)]
}

meths <- intersect(c("Screened_lin_honest", "GBLUP_loo", "GBLUP_nested", "TwoK_honest", "TwoK_oracle"), names(all_res))
meths <- c("RP_agg_old", meths)
R <- nrow(all_res)
summ <- data.frame(
  Method = meths,
  Mean_MSPE = sapply(meths, function(m) mean(all_res[[m]])),
  Diff_vs_aggTARP = sapply(meths, function(m) mean(all_res[[m]] - all_res$RP_agg_old)),
  SE = sapply(meths, function(m) sd(all_res[[m]] - all_res$RP_agg_old) / sqrt(R)),
  Beats_aggTARP = sapply(meths, function(m) sum(all_res[[m]] < all_res$RP_agg_old))
)
rownames(summ) <- NULL
knitr::kable(summ, digits = 2, caption = sprintf("%d seeds. TwoK_oracle peeks at the test set (diagnostic, not a method).", R))

d <- all_res$TwoK_honest - all_res$GBLUP_nested
cat(sprintf("\nTargeted GBLUP - GBLUP (both nested-tuned): mean %.2f, SE %.2f, targeted better in %d of %d seeds\n",
            mean(d), sd(d) / sqrt(R), sum(d < 0), R))
if ("GBLUP_loo" %in% names(all_res)) {
  d2 <- all_res$TwoK_honest - all_res$GBLUP_loo
  cat(sprintf("Targeted GBLUP - GBLUP (LOOCV, Experiment 0): mean %.2f, SE %.2f, targeted better in %d of %d seeds\n",
              mean(d2), sd(d2) / sqrt(R), sum(d2 < 0), R))
}
cat("\nw chosen by nested CV, counts over seeds:\n"); print(table(all_res$w_sel))
```

## 6. The w-curve: how much does a prior-variance boost on screened SNPs help?

```{r w-curve}
wcols <- paste0("T_w", W_GRID)
mu_w <- sapply(wcols, function(cn) mean(all_res[[cn]]))
dmat <- sapply(wcols, function(cn) all_res[[cn]] - all_res$T_w0)
wtab <- data.frame(w = W_GRID, prior_boost = 1 + W_GRID * p / mean(all_res$n_screened),
                   Mean_MSPE = mu_w, Diff_vs_w0 = colMeans(dmat),
                   SE = apply(dmat, 2, sd) / sqrt(R), Better_than_w0 = colSums(dmat < 0))
knitr::kable(wtab, digits = 2, caption = "Each w uses its own nested-CV lambda; w = 0 is GBLUP")

plot(seq_along(W_GRID), mu_w, type = "b", pch = 19, xaxt = "n", xlab = "w (weight on screened kernel)",
     ylab = "mean test MSPE", main = "Targeted GBLUP: MSPE vs w")
axis(1, at = seq_along(W_GRID), labels = W_GRID)
if ("Screened_lin_honest" %in% names(all_res)) abline(h = mean(all_res$Screened_lin_honest), col = "firebrick", lty = 3)
abline(h = mean(all_res$RP_agg_old), col = "darkgreen", lty = 3)
legend("topright", c("screened-only honest ridge", "aggregated TARP"), col = c("firebrick", "darkgreen"), lty = 3, bty = "n")
```

## 7. Does screening recover the known flowering-time loci? (seed 1, training rows only)

FRI (AT4G00650, chromosome 4) and FLC (AT5G10140, chromosome 5) are the classic large-effect
flowering-time loci. The positions below are **approximate TAIR10 coordinates typed from memory**
(FRI near 270 kb, FLC near 3.176 Mb): confirm them in TAIR before citing anything from this plot.

```{r manhattan}
set.seed(1)
tr1 <- sample(seq_len(n), size = round(0.8 * n))
gw1 <- big_univLinReg(G2, y.train = y_all[tr1], ind.train = tr1, ncores = N_CORES)
t1 <- gw1$estim / gw1$std.err
r1 <- sign(t1) * sqrt(t1^2 / (t1^2 + (length(tr1) - 2))); r1[is.na(r1)] <- 0

chr <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(map$chromosome)); pos <- map$physical.pos
ok <- !is.na(chr) & chr %in% 1:5
chr_len <- tapply(pos[ok], chr[ok], max)
off <- c(0, cumsum(as.numeric(chr_len))[-length(chr_len)]); names(off) <- names(chr_len)
xcum <- pos + off[as.character(chr)]
show <- ok & (abs(r1) > 0.15 | runif(p) < 0.05)
plot(xcum[show], abs(r1)[show], pch = 16, cex = 0.3, col = c("grey40", "steelblue")[chr[show] %% 2 + 1],
     xlab = "genome position (chromosomes 1-5 concatenated)", ylab = "|marginal correlation with FT10| (training rows)",
     main = "Marginal association of every SNP with flowering time")
fri <- off["4"] + 270000; flc <- off["5"] + 3176000
abline(v = c(fri, flc), col = "red", lty = 2)
text(c(fri, flc), max(abs(r1)), c("FRI (approx.)", "FLC (approx.)"), pos = 4, col = "red", cex = 0.8)

o <- order(abs(r1), decreasing = TRUE)[1:15]
top <- data.frame(chr = chr[o], pos = pos[o], r = round(r1[o], 3),
                  dist_to_FRI_bp = ifelse(chr[o] == 4, abs(pos[o] - 270000), NA),
                  dist_to_FLC_bp = ifelse(chr[o] == 5, abs(pos[o] - 3176000), NA))
knitr::kable(top, caption = "Top 15 SNPs by |r| (training rows, seed 1)")
```

## 8. How to read this

- **`TwoK_honest` clearly below `GBLUP_nested` (more than about 2 SE, most seeds):** TARP's targeted
  screening adds information beyond a dense kernel. That is the headline result, and the w-curve
  shows where the sweet spot sits.
- **They tie and `w` is mostly 0 or tiny:** the screened SNPs add nothing beyond GBLUP on this
  trait. That is a clean, well-controlled negative result and still worth reporting, together
  with the Experiment 0 finding.
- **The w-curve is U-shaped:** a moderate boost helps, and too much boost drifts toward the
  screened-only ridge (the dotted red line).
- **Manhattan plot:** if the strongest marginal signals sit on or near FRI / FLC, that is a
  biological sanity check on the screening step, and a presentable figure.
- Limits that still apply: one trait; the 10 splits share the same 1,003 accessions so SEs are
  optimistic; the screened set is a single Bernoulli draw per fold.
